author: Paul Dailing

access_notes: Read 2026-11-03 for T-3326 from the article page. It quotes the 1812 letters of the factor Matthew Irwin and the surgeon's mate Isaac Van Voorhis to the War Department and Captain Heald's reply to Irwin, which this project has not read in the original (they were published in the 1940s; the Wikipedia article on Jean La Lime cites the Ohio State Historical Society's Document Transcriptions of the War of 1812 in the Northwest, vol. VI, 1959, on HathiTrust, which this container cannot reach). So those letters are quoted here AS THE READER PRINTS THEM, and every claim says so.
note: LATER JOURNALISM THAT QUOTES THE CONTEMPORARY LETTERS. Its value is the 1812 letters it quotes and the land record it reports: that the Wayne County register at Detroit shows Lalime, not Le Mai, buying du Sable's post in 1800 with Kinzie as a witness, and that no record of the next transfer was found. Its framing is its own and openly partisan against the Kinzie family's version ('a popular lie'); claims that rest on its framing rather than on a quoted document are graded inferred, and the opposing versions are told beside it.
